title: Non-invasive and non-destructive measurements of confluence in cultured adherent cell lines
author: Busschots, O’Toole, et al.

steps.title: Prepare microscope and camera
steps.instruction: Set up the inverted Nikon (TMS) phase‑contrast microscope with the 4× objective lens in place. Attach the Nikon Coolpix 4500 camera using its lens adapter screwed onto the camera lens; remove one microscope eyepiece and insert the camera‑adapter assembly into the ocular tube. If using a different system, follow the camera’s user manual.

steps.title: Place cover slip and focus
steps.instruction: Remove the flask from the incubator and place the cardboard cover slip (designed to fit the flask bottom and containing 1 cm holes near the top and bottom) onto the flask bottom. Position the 4× objective over a hole and adjust focus until cell nuclei are sharply visible on the camera LCD screen (cytoplasm may be slightly out of focus).

steps.title: Capture top and bottom images
steps.instruction: Zoom the Nikon Coolpix camera to an aperture of F4.0 (or an equivalent setting that reproduces the appearance shown in Fig. 2a). Take one photograph through the top hole and one through the bottom hole of the cover slip. For evenly dispersed cells any location within the 1 cm² hole is acceptable; for clumped cells photograph the largest colony within that area.

steps.title: Return flask to incubator
steps.instruction: Place the flask back into the incubator immediately after imaging.

steps.title: Transfer images to computer
steps.instruction: Copy the JPEG images generated by the Nikon Coolpix 4500 to a computer for analysis. ImageJ can read JPEG as well as TIFF, GIF, PNG, DICOM, BMP, PGM and FITS formats.

steps.title: Process image in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Analyze each photograph using ImageJ 1.45s following the sequence below.

substeps.instruction: Subtract background (Process → Subtract Background…): set Rolling ball radius = 20.0 pixels, tick Light background and Preview, then OK.
Adjust threshold (Image → Adjust → Threshold…): set the lower threshold bar between 65528 and 65532 (choose the value giving best coverage) and click Apply.
Set measurements (Analyze → Set Measurements): tick Area, Standard deviation, Min & max gray value, Integrated density, Area fraction, Mean gray value, Perimeter, Median.
Analyze particles (Analyze → Analyze Particles…): set Size = 100‑Infinity, Circularity = 0.00‑1.00, Show = Outlines; tick Display results, Summarize and Include holes; click OK.
Save the Results and Summary tables as Excel worksheets. The Summary file contains the “area fraction” (percentage of image area covered by cells).

steps.title: Check analysis accuracy
steps.instruction: Overlay the generated outline image onto the original to verify correct cell identification.

substeps.instruction: Select the generated image from step g (e.g., “Drawing of X.JPG”).
Invert image (Image → Lookup Tables → Invert LUT).
Change colour to red (Image → Lookup Tables → Red).
Invert image again (Image → Lookup Tables → Invert LUT).
Convert both original and generated images to RGB colour (Image → Type → RGB Colour).
Merge images (Process → Image Calculator…): Image1 = Original image, Operation = Add, Image2 = Generated image, tick Create new window, then OK.

If the overlay shows red outlines matching cell edges, save the merged image as accurate. If not, return to step d (threshold) and/or step g (size) in the analysis and repeat until a good fit is obtained.

steps.title: Analyse second photograph and average AF
steps.instruction: Repeat the full ImageJ analysis (steps 6‑8) for the second photograph (top or bottom). Record the area fraction (AF) from each Summary file and calculate the average of the two AF values; this average represents confluence for the entire flask.

steps.title: Interpret area fraction
steps.instruction: An average AF ≥ 30 % indicates a confluent T‑25 flask for OVCAR8 and UPN251 cells. Adjust the cut‑off value as needed for other cell lines.

steps.title: Validate AF with cell counts (optional)
steps.instruction: Plate OVCAR8 or UPN251 cells into eight T‑25 flasks at 2.6 × 10⁴ cells per flask. After 24 h incubation, photograph two flasks and calculate AF as above, then trypsinise those flasks and count cells with a haemocytometer. Repeat for subsequent 24 h intervals. Correlate AF values with haemocytometer counts using Spearman correlation (n = 3 replicates; reported r = 0.99 ± 0.008 for OVCAR8 and 0.99 ± 0.01 for UPN251, p = 0.01).

steps.title: Apply AF to drug‑recovery experiments (optional)
steps.instruction: Plate cells at 2.6 × 10⁴ cells per T‑25 flask. On day 2 add carboplatin (2 µg ml⁻¹ for UPN251, 4 µg ml⁻¹ for OVCAR8). Remove drug‑containing media on day 5 and replace with fresh drug‑free media. Monitor confluence daily using the AF method; when AF indicates confluence, reseed cells into T‑75 flasks. After a ≥4‑week recovery period repeat the drug exposure cycle. Record AF values each round to track decreasing recovery times.

description: OVCAR8 and UPN251 cells were plated into eight T-25 flasks at a cell density of 2.6 × 104 cells per flask. The flasks were left in an incubator for 24 h to allow cells to attach. After this time two of the flasks were removed and photographed, followed by AF output calculation. The two flasks were then trypsinised and cells counted using a haemocytometer. The remaining flasks were incubated and the same procedure was used over subsequent 24 h periods. AF output data was compared to cell count data using a Spearman correlation to see if the data sets correlated. AF calculation was found to be highly correlated with cell count results using a haemocytometer. The average correlation co-efficient value obtained from a Spearman correlation test for n = 3 replicates was 0.99 ± 0.008 for OVCAR8 and 0.99 ± 0.01 for UPN251 with a p-value of 0.01 for both cell lines. See Fig. 4. This shows that AF calculation is a reliable measure for surface area cover of cells within a T25 flask and that this corresponds to cell count.
